title: EvoDS: Self-Evolving Autonomous Data Science Agent with Skill Learning and Context Management

problem.claim: Automated data science agents need to operate reliably in multi-stage, iterative pipelines.

gap.claim: Existing approaches have static action sets and lack principled long-horizon context management, limiting reusable experience across tasks.

contributions.claim: EvoDS is a self-evolving autonomous data science agent that expands its skills and manages long-term context through agentic reinforcement learning.
The Autonomous Skill Acquisition mechanism synthesizes, validates, and reuses executable skills, while Adaptive Context Compression treats context management as a learned control problem.
A two-stage multi-agent training scheme orchestrates the proposed strategies for autonomous improvement over time.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that EvoDS's hierarchical design reduces tool-selection error and that its optimization objective aligns with an information bottleneck principle.
The authors report a 28.9% average improvement over state-of-the-art open-source data science agents across four diverse benchmarks.
The authors report eliminating out-of-token failures and making code and data available.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLM agents have enabled advances in automated data science.
Existing agents are constrained by static actions and weak long-horizon context management.
EvoDS addresses the gap through skill expansion and adaptive long-term context management.
The strategies are coordinated through two-stage multi-agent training and supported by theoretical claims about error reduction and efficient context use.
The authors report benchmark gains, elimination of out-of-token failures, and release of code and data.

source_observation.claim: EvoDS combines executable-skill reuse with learned context compression for iterative data science pipelines.

interpretation.claim: Separating reusable capabilities from context-control decisions may help agents handle long-horizon workflows.

application.claim: Agent systems for multi-stage workflows could consider explicit skill libraries and learned policies for retaining or compressing context.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this design transfers beyond the reported data science setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the four benchmarks, baselines, datasets, or evaluation protocol.
The abstract does not provide quantitative details for tool-selection error, context efficiency, or out-of-token failures.
The abstract does not describe the reinforcement-learning objective, training data, or implementation details.
